title: Therapeutic mechanisms of iPSC-MSC derived extracellular vesicles on dry mouth caused by Sjorgren's syndrome or radiotherapy
text:
Long term dry mouth is common in patients with Sjögren's syndrome or treated with
radiation therapy for head and neck cancers and is difficult to remedy. This proposal aims
to determine therapeutic mechanisms of extracellular vesicles generated by induced
pluripotent stem cell derived mesenchymal stem cells on these two types of dry mouth.
The success of proposed research will provide the proof-of-concept and the guide of
optimization for novel and clinically feasible therapies of these two types of dry mouth,
which will also encourage further research on similar therapies for other autoimmune
diseases or radiation damages.

title: Acquisition of an automated robotic culture system for organoid generation, maintenance, and phenotyping
text:
This project seeks to enhance the capabilities of the Emory Organoid Hub by acquiring a Molecular Devices
CellXpress.ai, an automated organoid cell culture system, to improve the standardization, scalability, and
reproducibility of 3D organoid models. By reducing variability and lowering costs, this system will advance
research in human biology and disease, benefiting a wide range of scientific investigations and collaborations at
Emory and beyond, in line with NIH's mission and scientific priorities.

title: Personalizing Veterans' Lung Cancer Screening and Diagnosis
text:
Lung cancer screening with low-dose chest computed tomography (CT) is currently recommended for high-risk
individuals who are 50 to 80 years old, have smoked cigarettes for at least 20 pack-years, and currently smoke
or quit smoking within the past 15 years. In a prospective cohort at Nashville, Denver and Louisville Veteran
Affairs medical centers, we will evaluate the detection of lung cancer using new lung cancer screening eligibility
criteria based on Veterans' personal and service-related exposures compared to standard of care criteria.
Screening a larger population will increase the number of lung nodules needing clinical management and these
nodules may or may not be cancer. In a population of Veterans with positive screenings at Nashville, we will also
validate a combination biomarker-based approach to manage screen-detected lung nodules to reduce time to
lung cancer diagnosis in nodules that are cancer and use of invasive procedures in nodules that are not cancer.

title: Engineer A Chemogenetic Toolbox for Unraveling Complex Signaling Networks
text:
Immunotherapy, notably with agents targeting PD-1/PD-L1 and CTLA-4/B7-1, has significantly advanced cancer
treatment, yet its efficacy is restricted to a subset of patients, highlighting the need to explore additional immune
targets such as TIGIT signaling. To address the limited effectiveness of anti-TIGIT monotherapy in clinical trials,
we propose to create an innovative chemogenetic toolbox for the detailed analysis of TIGIT interactions or
crosstalk and to develop a quantitative model that accurately captures both individual and collective pathway
dynamics. This endeavor will shed light on the complex interplay and crosstalk within the TIGIT signaling network,
offering a strategic framework to identify highly effective therapeutic target combinations and significantly expand
the capabilities of cancer immunotherapy.

title: Ethical Considerations and Barriers to Generalizable Evidence and Data Sharing for Individualized Genomic Therapies
text:
The goal of this research is to use empirical bioethics methods to generate
consensus and recommendations related to the development of individualized genomic therapies. Specifically,
this project characterizes ethical considerations and logistical barriers to effective evidence generation and
data sharing for n-of-1 therapeutics by conducting in-depth interviews with key contributors, analyzing
published literature on this topic, and conducting a Delphi study to build consensus among experts in the field.
This work will culminate in a set of recommendations to ensure ethical evidence generation and data sharing
for individualized genomic therapies.

title: TRPM8 in eye health and disease
text:
Project Relevance
Dry eye disease, ocular pain and ocular discomfort present significant challenges to our quality of life. There
has been recent interest in therapeutics directly targeting the activity of ocular cold sensory neurons, due to
their key involvement in eye physiology, dry eye disease and ocular discomfort. Our proposal aims to dissect
the function and activation mechanisms of the cold and menthol receptor TRPM8, a critical thermosensitive
component of ocular cold sensory neurons, which will set the stage for the development of novel drugs to
combat dry eye disease and ocular pain.

title: Follicular Regulatory T-cells Promote Cancer
text:
This study aims to reveal the previously unappreciated cell type, TFR cells, as a cancer prognostic marker and
the IgE response as a predictor to the disrupted TFR cell function. This study will also illustrate how adaptive
immunity interplays with innate responses contributing to tumor evolution. If successful, this study would advance
our fundamental mechanistic understanding of tumor immunology and lead to a new direction for cancer
immunotherapy.

title: Genetic and Functional Mechanisms in Citrate Transporter Disorder associated with SLC13A5
text:
The proposed research will further our understanding of SLC13A5-associated citrate transporter disorder by
establishing and characterizing Drosophila and mouse models for the disease. These studies will provide
evidence supporting the complexity of SLC13A5 disease mechanisms as well as designing potential therapies
for this disorder. Using our novel models, our multidisciplinary approach will characterize phenotype-genotype
relationships and molecular mechanisms underlying SLC13A5 disease, and use the power of Drosophila
genetics to design new therapeutic strategies.

title: Tryptophan-kynurenine pathway PET imaging in human gliomas.
text:
In this translational imaging proposal, we evaluate the clinical use of a novel, clinically feasible amino acid
(tryptophan-based) molecular imaging approach to assess newly-diagnosed and recurrent gliomas in adult
patients. This imaging approach has the potential to improve accurate glioma detection to facilitate targeted
treatment (surgery and radiation) and also monitor drug treatment targeting abnormal tryptophan metabolism
and aiming at reversing tumoral immune resistance, with the ultimate goal of improving clinical outcomes.

title: High Performance, Quantitative Breast PET Scanner Integrated With Tomosynthesis
text:
A dedicated breast PET-DBT scanner provides higher spatial resolution and sensitivity PET images
compared to a clinical PET/CT scanner, that are co-registered to DBT images. The co-registered
quantitative molecular and anatomical images can play an important role in breast cancer treatment -
ranging from diagnostic breast imaging through surgical planning to systemic treatment.

title: Engineered Colon Cancer Tissue to Examine the Role of the Obese Microenvironment in Tumor Aggressiveness
text:
The tissue engineered platforms developed and validated in the proposed project will be extremely valuable to
the understanding and eventual treatment of colorectal cancer (CRC) linked to obesity. The portability of these
tissue engineered platforms to other obesity-linked cancers and cancer in general has the potential to inform
and shift current research and clinical practice.

title: Building machine learning models to identify placental causes of stillbirth
text:
Stillbirth, loss of the fetus after 20 weeks of gestation, is a devastating pregnancy outcome for
families, obstetricians, and midwives. Examination of the placenta, the fetal life support organ
during pregnancy, is the single most important step in identifying the cause of stillbirth, yet most
placentas are examined by non-experts. We propose developing machine learning models to
identify placental causes of stillbirth, which we envision being used by obstetricians and non-
expert pathologists in guiding patients and identifying & treating those at risk of stillbirth in a
subsequent pregnancy.

title: Genomic- informed development of a cheap, portable assay to rapidly profile drug-resistant bacterial infections
text:
Antibiotic-resistant bacterial infections are one of the leading causes of mortality worldwide with an especially
high burden in low-resource environments, where the medical infrastructure necessary to detect them is limited;
novel diagnostics are urgently required to address this gap. The investigators have collected a large cohort of
highly resistant clinical isolates from Peru which will undergo whole-genome sequencing with comparison to
other sequenced cohorts to assess shared porin mutations, and have simultaneously developed a prototype
assay capable of rapidly diagnosing bacterial infections of the bloodstream. In this proposal, they will use insights
from the analysis of the bacterial genomes to enhance the clinical utility of their assay, deepen our understanding
of the genetic drivers of resistance, and validate a novel platform to detect resistant infections in low-resource
settings.

title: Fluorescence lifetime imaging for quantitative assessment of in vivo PD-L1 target engagement.
text:
This R21 application introduces a translational imaging strategy that employs fluorescence lifetime (FL) imaging
of a near-infrared (NIR) fluorophore labeled PD-L1 antibody (Atezolizumab-IRDye800CW, “Atezo-800”) to
noninvasively measure PD-L1 target engagement in head and neck cancer. Our preliminary data show that the
FL of antibody-conjugated NIR dyes increases upon specific target binding in the tumor microenvironment,
enabling clear discrimination between bound and unbound probes. By providing a robust, noninvasive measure
of PD-L1–bound antibody, FL imaging of Atezo-800 could offer immediate applications in patient stratification,
dose optimization, and the advancement of next-generation immunotherapies.

title: Hippocampal Vulnerability to Environmental Pesticide Exposure
text:
Evidence indicates that early-life environmental exposure to pyrethroids, such as deltamethrin (DM), at no-
adverse observed-effect level (NOAEL), increases the risk of neurodevelopmental disorders. Building on
groundbreaking results that demonstrate the effects of early-life DM exposure on hippocampal function and
memory formation, we will provide new insights into the mechanisms of DM neurotoxicity and identify
countermeasures to mitigate the risk of exposure.

title: Understanding the Role of rRNA modifications in Colon Cancer
text:
There is an emerging field in cancer biology exploring how specialized ribosomes contribute to the
development and progression of cancers, but little is understood about how they alter the protein
dosage of genes that support cancer survival. The overall goal of this proposal is to discover how a
subset of special ribosomes that are increased in colon cancer contributes to a protein synthesis
network that supports colon cancer growth and survival. Understanding how colon cancers are
coordinating a selective translation program will unveil novel post-transcriptional mechanisms of gene
regulation and elucidate avenues for therapeutic intervention in the disease.

title: Enhancement and optimization of a mobile iBCI for Veterans with paralysis
text:
VA research has been advancing a high-performance brain-computer interface (BCI) to improve
independence for Veterans and others living with tetraplegia or the inability to speak resulting
from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, spinal cord injury or stoke. In supervised research sessions,
iBCI technology has enabled individuals with severe paralysis to use computers by imagining
their own hand movements to control point-and-click actions for on-screen typing, browsing the
web and other familiar enabling activities. In this project, we enhance deep learning neural
network decoders and multi-state gesture decoding for increased accuracy and reliability and
deploy them on a battery-powered mobile BCI device for independent use of computers and
touch-enabled mobile devices at home.

title: UC Davis Multi-Disciplinary Cancer Research Training Program to Advance Precision Cancer Prevention and Care in Latin America.
text:
The UC Davis Multidisciplinary Research Training Program to Advance Precision Cancer
Medicine aims to create a globally engaged research workforce in cancer genomics and longterm collaborative pipelines. This program aims to strengthen U.S. scientific leadership,
accelerate innovation in cancer genetics and precision medicine, and contribute to improved
public health cancer outcomes for diverse U.S. populations.

title: Metabolic Symbiosis: Lactate as an Epigenetic Regulator and a Biofuel in Age-dependent Intervertebral Disc Degeneration
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it investigates the role of a new
pathway in intervertebral disc degeneration and low back pain. The proposed studies aim to
confirm the important roles of lactate as an important source for disc nutrition and gene
regulation. If confirmed, it will provide a new research direction to identify novel therapeutic
targets for this common and costly condition.

title: ILLUMINE
text: Cells produce a previously under-appreciated class of non-standard proteins collectively termed the dark proteome that are not encoded by known open reading frames or explained by DNA mutations. The biological origins, regulation, and functional role of the dark proteome in normal tissues and cancer remain largely unknown. This challenge aims to uncover the mechanisms that give rise to dark proteome products and to define their connection to the oncogenic state. Team ILLUMINE led by Reuven Agami (Netherlands Cancer Institute) brings together interdisciplinary researchers with expertise in cancer biology, proteomics, genomics, chemistry, technology development, and clinical translation. The program will address four central questions: who the dark proteome players are, whether and how they are (dys)regulated in cancer, how they function, and how they can be therapeutically exploited. In addressing these questions, ILLUMINE will address major gaps in knowledge. Aim 1 will create a comprehensive map of dark proteome entities across several major cancer types and dissect potential stress-related mechanisms for their production. Aim 2 will codify a bench-to-bedside pre-clinical therapeutic development pipeline for immunotherapies from the dark proteome. Aim 3 will profile cell-based mechanisms of individual dark proteins in cancer biology, focusing on cell autonomous and non-cell autonomous mechanisms. Aim 4 will explore non-immunotherapy opportunities for targeting the dark proteome. Capitalizing on its unique expertise, the team plans to use and combine cutting-edge experimental approaches to uncover hidden layers of cancer cell biology. ILLUMINE aims to ultimately identify new tumor biology and treatment paradigms for patients based on the dark proteome.
